subject: Re: Dedicated capacity shortfall for LumenAI May surge
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire@lumenai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity shortfall for LumenAI May surge

Hannah / Marissa,

We're running into a material shortfall for the May production surge. Our telemetry and upcoming marketing campaign indicate a peak that will require ~32 A100-equivalent GPU slots for roughly 3-4 weeks starting week of May 24. Current Dedicated reservation only covers ~12 GPUs, and our latency SLOs degrade sharply beyond that.

Can Redwood provide headroom or a temporary tranche increase? If not, we need to understand fallbacks (queued/burst, lower-tier quantized model, or rate-limiting) so we can notify product and PR. I've attached our demand forecast (CSV) and included a quick summary below: 
- Baseline: 12 GPUs (reserved)
- Projected peak: 32 GPUs (24–36 sustained over 24/7 windows)
- Critical window: 2028-05-24 to 2028-06-18

We appreciate quick transparency on options and timelines — customer execs are asking for a clear plan today.

Thanks,
Claire Donovan
Head of Platform
LumenAI
(attached: Lumen_Demand_Forecast_MAY2028.csv)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity shortfall for LumenAI May surge

Claire — thanks for the flag and for the forecast. Marissa and I will review immediately. Looping in Ben (CS) and Karthik (Capacity) so we can assess headroom and potential reallocations.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether 24 GPUs (a middle option) would keep you within acceptable latency bounds if we apply prefix caching and lower-precision quantization for non-critical workloads? That helps us prioritize which workloads must remain on full-precision instances.

I can carve out 30 minutes for a triage call this afternoon (2:30pm PT). If that works, we'll bring a proposed mutual action plan.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

On 2028-05-19 09:12, Claire Donovan wrote:
> Hannah / Marissa,
>
> We're running into a material shortfall for the May production surge...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@lumenai.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity shortfall for LumenAI May surge

Claire — appreciate the data. I ran a quick model against your forecast and sketched a mutual action plan below; attaching the CSV back with annotations.

Proposed immediate steps (MAY window):
1) Short-term tranche increase: allocate 16 additional GPUs from our reserved headroom for 4 weeks (target start 2028-05-24).
2) Burst allowance: allow up to 24 GPUs for sustained windows via burst credits during peak hours (evenings PT).
3) Quality guardrails: require the customer to run non-critical batch/analytics on int8 variants where possible — we can help with conversion guides.
4) Commercial: one-time amendment to DL-4821 to cover incremental usage + a good-faith credit for any outage risk.

Trade-offs to surface: the tranche increase reduces immediate headroom for other deals; we need infra confirmation on preemptibility and fallback order.

Attachment: Lumen_Demand_Forecast_MAY2028.csv (annotated).

If you approve, we'll draft an amendment and a short-run SLO addendum. Meeting at 2:30pm PT confirmed unless you prefer earlier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity shortfall for LumenAI May surge — allocation options

Team — I ran a capacity check across the US Dedicated fleet and drafted three feasible allocation options. Attachment: allocation_matrix_v3.xlsx

Option A (Conservative) — minimal risk to other customers
- Provide +8 GPUs to Lumen (total 20) by reassigning queued burst pool
- Impact: no SLA changes for other deals; Lumen may need to degrade non-critical paths

Option B (Balanced) — recommended
- Provide +16 GPUs (total 28) by temporarily reallocating 12 GPUs from lower-priority tranche (SunriseMed DL-4390) and 4 GPUs from pooled headroom
- Impact: SunriseMed notified of preemption window; minimal expected SLA impact if scheduled properly

Option C (Aggressive) — full peak coverage
- Provide +24 GPUs (total 36) by shifting reserved capacity across regions and reducing burst availability platform-wide
- Impact: higher risk to multiple low-priority customers; requires exec approval and commercial crediting

Notes:
- Reallocation window must be set with explicit start/end and automatic rollback to avoid prolonged drift.
- We can enable prefix caching and int8 fallbacks to reduce required slot count by ~20% for some paths; that can be negotiated into the amendment.

I'll attach the matrix with device-level slots and timelines. Need a decision on which option before 2028-05-21 15:00 PT to meet Lumen's requested start date.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Capacity Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: LumenAI surge — allocation decision required

Rishi / Laura — escalating for decision. Lumen is their biggest remaining pilot partner for Q2 and the request is timeboxed: start 2028-05-24. Summary of options below (from Karthik):
- A: +8 GPUs (conservative)
- B: +16 GPUs (balanced — recommended)
- C: +24 GPUs (aggressive)

Commercial ask (from Marissa): one-time amendment to DL-4821 and a small credit tied to any performance impact.

Key considerations for decision:
- Business: Lumen's expansion velocity and strategic visibility for next quarter; losing momentum risks churn on a high-touch pilot.
- Infra: preemption impact on SunriseMed (DL-4390) and a hard rollback window is required.
- Finance: short-term revenue vs. long-term partnership value.

Asking for a call or a quick thumbs by 15:00 PT today. If we choose B, operations will execute a hot reassign and Marissa will draft the amendment.

Context (attachments): annotated forecast, allocation matrix.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: LumenAI surge — allocation decision required

Thanks for the clear summary. After weighing commercial and operational risk, we approve Option B (Balanced) with these guardrails:
1) Temporary reallocation of 12 GPUs from SunriseMed (DL-4390) for the window 2028-05-24 to 2028-06-18; automated rollback at 06:00 PT on 2028-06-19.
2) Lumen to accept a performance mitigation plan: enable int8 for non-latency-critical paths and prefix caching where possible. Redwood SRE to run verification tests prior to cutover.
3) Commercial: Marissa to prepare an amendment (DL-4821-A1) with a one-time usage surcharge and a small credit to Lumen for the operational risk. Signatures via DocuSign (DOCUSIGN-12345).

Ben — please coordinate the rollback automation. Karthik — execute the reassign and share the final allocation_matrix_v3.xlsx with exact device IDs and timings. Marissa — send the amendment to Claire and copy legal.

I'll join the post-cutover check on 2028-05-25. Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
(attachment: signed_amendment_docusign.pdf)
